15.solution:

\[\rho' = \rho_{0}\cdot\frac{P'}{P_{0}}\cdot\frac{T_{0}}{T'} = \rho_{0}\cdot\frac{3P_{0}}{P_{0}}\cdot\frac{T_{0}}{2T_{0}} = \frac{3}{2}\rho_{0}.\]

Among the options, \(\mathrm{Cd}\) is the soft metal.

57.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
57.solution: For the elementary reaction \(\mathrm{O_3 + O \to 2O_2}\) with rate \(= k[\mathrm{O_3}][\mathrm{O}]\), order \(= 1 + 1 = 2\). For an elementary reaction molecularity equals the number of reactant species colliding \(= 2\). So order \(2\) and molecularity \(2\).

58.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
58.solution: The movement of charged colloidal particles towards the oppositely charged electrode under an applied potential is called electrophoresis.

59.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
59.solution: Standard free energy change \(\Delta G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}_{cell}\) depends on the amount of substance \((n)\), so it is an extensive property, not intensive. Hence statement C is false. (Standard cell potential is intensive; electrode potential depends on concentration; electrical work \(= -\Delta G\) — all true.)

60.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
60.solution: Pressure-volume work for a gaseous reaction at constant \(T\): \(W = -\Delta n_g RT\). For \(\mathrm{4SO_2 + 2O_2 \to 4SO_3}\), \(\Delta n_g = 4 - (4+2) = -2\). \(W = -(-2)\times 8.314 \times 300 = 4988.4\ \mathrm{J}\).

61.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
61.solution: The green-chemistry principle that recommends using chemicals derived from plant/renewable (rather than petroleum) sources is 'Use of renewable feedstocks'.

62.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
62.solution: By the Irving-Williams series, the stability of high-spin divalent first-row transition-metal complexes follows \(\mathrm{Mn^{2+} < Fe^{2+} < Co^{2+} < Ni^{2+} < Cu^{2+}}\). With the same ligand, \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) forms the most stable complex.

63.subtopic: Oxidation State, Coordination Number and IUPAC Nomenclature
63.solution: Stock notation puts the oxidation state in Roman numerals. Aurous chloride is \(\mathrm{Au(I)Cl}\) (Au is \(+1\)); writing it as \(\mathrm{Au(III)Cl_3}\) is wrong (that is auric chloride). Hence statement D is NOT correct.

64.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life
64.solution: For a first-order reaction the time to halve the concentration is the half-life, \(t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k} = \dfrac{0.693}{1.386\times 10^{-3}} = 500\ \mathrm{s}\).
64.stemOverride: Calculate the time in seconds required to reduce the concentration of reactant to half of initial concentration for first order reaction if rate constant is \(1.386 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}\).
64.note: Stem rate constant lost its leading digit in extraction ('.386' \(\to\) intended \(1.386\times10^{-3}\)); restored so the answer 500 s (= 0.693/k) is reproducible. Key D correct.

66.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
66.solution: The characteristic and most stable oxidation state of the lanthanoids is \(+3\). With \(\mathrm{OH^{-}}\) the hydroxide is therefore \(\mathrm{Ln(OH)_3}\).

67.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
67.solution: Boiling point reflects strength of intermolecular H-bonding. Carboxylic acids form the strongest (dimeric) H-bonds via the very polar \(\mathrm{O{-}H}\) of \(-\mathrm{COOH}\); alcohols H-bond through \(\mathrm{O{-}H}\); amines have a less polar \(\mathrm{N{-}H}\) so the weakest H-bonding. Order: carboxylic acids > alcohols > amines.

68.solution: Thermosetting polymers are cross-linked and set irreversibly on heating. Urea-formaldehyde resin is a thermosetting polymer. Polyvinyl, polystyrene and nylon-6,6 are thermoplastics.

69.subtopic: IUPAC Nomenclature, Functional Groups and Homologous Series
69.solution: The seniority order of principal characteristic groups is \(-\mathrm{COOH} > -\mathrm{SO_3H} > -\mathrm{COOR} > -\mathrm{COCl} > -\mathrm{CONH_2} > -\mathrm{CN} > -\mathrm{CHO} > >\!{C}{=}{O} > -\mathrm{OH}\). Among the given groups \((-\mathrm{COCl}, -\mathrm{SO_3H}, -\mathrm{CHO}, -\mathrm{OH})\), \(-\mathrm{SO_3H}\) has the highest priority.

70.subtopic: Crystal Defects, Magnetic Properties and Semiconductors
70.solution: When the cation-to-anion ratio differs from that given by the formula, the crystal is non-stoichiometric; this is a nonstoichiometric defect (e.g. metal excess/deficiency).

71.solution: A phenolic \(-\mathrm{OH}\) is attached directly to an aromatic ring. Curcumin, eugenol and gallic acid all bear phenolic \(-\mathrm{OH}\) groups on benzene rings. Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is an enediol on a furanone ring with no \(-\mathrm{OH}\) on a benzene ring, so it has no phenolic \(-\mathrm{OH}\).

72.solution: Depression of freezing point depends on the total molality of particles after dissociation. NaCl: \(0.1\times 2 = 0.2\); \(\mathrm{MgSO_4}\): \(0.05\times 2 = 0.10\); \(\mathrm{AlPO_4}\): \(0.08\times 2 = 0.16\); \(\mathrm{Al_2(SO_4)_3}\): \(0.06\times 5 = 0.30\). The smallest particle molality (\(0.10\), for \(\mathrm{MgSO_4}\)) gives the lowest depression.

73.subtopic: Reactions of Alkenes, Addition, Oxidation and Ozonolysis
73.solution: Acidic \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) \((\mathrm{KMnO_4 / dil.\ H_2SO_4})\) is a strong oxidant that cleaves the \(\mathrm{C{=}C}\). A terminal \(=\mathrm{CH}-\) carbon is oxidised all the way to a carboxylic acid (alkanoic acid); a \(=\mathrm{CH_2}\) ends up as \(\mathrm{CO_2}\). The characteristic product is an alkanoic acid.

74.solution: \(\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S\). For spontaneity only at high temperature, the \(-T\Delta S\) term must make \(\Delta G\) negative as \(T\) rises, which requires \(\Delta H > 0\) and \(\Delta S > 0\) (endothermic, entropy-driven).

75.solution: Energy of one photon \(E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \dfrac{(6.626\times 10^{-34})(3\times 10^{8})}{700\times 10^{-9}} = 2.839\times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}\). Per mole \(= 2.839\times 10^{-19} \times 6.022\times 10^{23} = 1.71\times 10^{5}\ \mathrm{J}\).

76.solution: Lone pairs on the central atom: \(\mathrm{SCl_2}\) (S, 2 lp), \(\mathrm{PCl_3}\) (P, 1 lp), \(\mathrm{ClF_3}\) (Cl, 2 lp), \(\mathrm{XeF_4}\) (Xe, 2 lp). The minimum is in \(\mathrm{PCl_3}\) with 1 lone pair.

77.subtopic: SI Units, Physical Properties and Atomic Abundance
77.solution: Rate of diffusion \(= \dfrac{\text{volume of gas diffused}}{\text{time}}\). With volume in \(\mathrm{dm^3}\) and time in \(\mathrm{s}\), the unit is \(\mathrm{dm^3\,s^{-1}}\).

78.solution: Nitric oxide \((\mathrm{NO})\), like the oxides of nitrogen \((\mathrm{NO_x})\) and chlorofluorocarbons, catalyses the destruction of stratospheric ozone: \(\mathrm{NO + O_3 \to NO_2 + O_2}\). He, \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{H_2}\) do not deplete ozone. Hence NO.

79.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy
79.solution: Standard enthalpy of formation is per mole of compound. The given reaction forms 2 mol \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) with \(\Delta_r H^{\circ} = -92.0\ \mathrm{kJ}\), so \(\Delta_f H^{\circ}(\mathrm{NH_3}) = \dfrac{-92.0}{2} = -46.0\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}\).

80.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
80.solution: The structure is a cyclobutane ring bearing \(-\mathrm{OH}\) on one carbon (C1) with an ethyl group on the adjacent C2 and a methyl group on C4. As a saturated cyclic alcohol the parent is cyclobutanol (\(-\mathrm{OH}\) gives C1, no '-ene'). Lowest locants give 2-ethyl-4-methylcyclobutanol. Options A and B are wrong (they call it a cyclobutene/hydroxy-substituent), and D gives higher locants.
80.note: Stem diagram (cyclobutanol with ethyl on C2 and methyl on C4) read to solve. Options are text IUPAC names; no figures to attach.

81.solution: The Fittig reaction couples two aryl halides with sodium in dry ether to give a biaryl: \(\mathrm{2C_6H_5Cl + 2Na \to C_6H_5{-}C_6H_5 + 2NaCl}\). Option B (both reactants aryl halides) is the Fittig reaction. Option A is Wurtz, C is Wurtz-Fittig, D is a mixed Wurtz.

82.subtopic: Nomenclature and Classification of Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
82.solution: The structure is a benzene ring carrying \(-\mathrm{CHO}\), \(-\mathrm{OH}\) and \(-\mathrm{CH_3}\), all meta to one another. The senior group \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) defines the parent (benzaldehyde, C1). The \(-\mathrm{OH}\) (hydroxy) and \(-\mathrm{CH_3}\) (methyl) get the lowest locant set \(\{3,5\}\). IUPAC name: 3-hydroxy-5-methylbenzaldehyde. (Naming it as a phenol, as in A/B, is wrong because \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) outranks \(-\mathrm{OH}\).)
82.note: Stem diagram (1,3,5-trisubstituted benzene: CHO, OH, CH3) read to solve. Options are text IUPAC names; no figures to attach.

83.subtopic: Nomenclature, Structural Isomers and Physical Properties
83.solution: Among isomeric \(\mathrm{C_6H_{14}}\) alkanes, the straight chain has the largest surface area and strongest London forces, hence the highest boiling point. n-Hexane (unbranched) boils highest; branching (2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,2-dimethylbutane) lowers it.

85.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
85.solution: For the oxidation \(\mathrm{Mg(s) \to Mg^{2+}(0.1\,M) + 2e^{-}}\), the oxidation potential is \(-\) the reduction potential. Reduction potential \(E = E^{\circ} - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log\dfrac{1}{[\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}]} = -2.37 - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log\dfrac{1}{0.1} = -2.37 - 0.0296 = -2.3996\ \mathrm{V}\). The oxidation (electrode) potential \(= +2.3996\ \mathrm{V}\).

86.solution: Interhalogens \(\mathrm{XX'_n}\) have \(n = 1, 3, 5, 7\) (always odd), e.g. \(\mathrm{ClF_3, BrF_5, IF_7}\). They are covalent, diamagnetic, and more reactive than the parent halogens (except \(\mathrm{F_2}\)). The false statement is D ('number of \(X'\) atoms is always even').

87.solution: Density \(\rho = \dfrac{n\,m}{a^3}\) where \(m\) is the mass of one atom and \(n\) atoms per cell. With \(\rho a^3 = 1.792\times 10^{-22}\ \mathrm{g}\) and \(m = 4.4\times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{g}\): \(n = \dfrac{\rho a^3}{m} = \dfrac{1.792\times 10^{-22}}{4.4\times 10^{-23}} = 4.07 \approx 4\). \(n = 4\) corresponds to a face-centred cubic (fcc) unit cell.
87.stemOverride: The mass of an atom present in unit cell is \(4.4 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{g}\) and the product of density and volume of unit cell is \(1.792 \times 10^{-22}\ \mathrm{g}\). What is the type of cubic unit cell?
87.note: Stem '\(\rho V\)' lost its leading digit in extraction ('.792' \(\to\) intended \(1.792\times10^{-22}\)); restored so n = 4 (fcc) is reproducible. Key B correct.

88.solution: Essential amino acids cannot be synthesised in the human body and must come from diet. Tryptophan is an essential amino acid. Tyrosine, glutamine and glycine are non-essential (can be synthesised). Hence tryptophan.

89.subtopic: Oxidation State, Coordination Number and IUPAC Nomenclature
89.solution: Cisplatin is \(\mathrm{cis\text{-}[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]}\): two \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) and two \(\mathrm{Cl^{-}}\) unidentate ligands bind Pt(II). The coordination number is 4.

90.subtopic: pH, pOH and Ionic Product of Water

91.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
91.solution: For the Zn-Ag cell, \(n = 2\). Maximum electrical work \(= -nFE^{\circ}_{cell} = -(2)(96500)(1.55) = -299150\ \mathrm{J} = -299.15\ \mathrm{kJ}\) (negative, work done by the system).

92.solution: 3,4-Dibromohexane is \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2{-}CHBr{-}CHBr{-}CH_2CH_3}\). C3 is bonded to \(\mathrm{C_2H_5}\), Br, H and the C4 fragment; C4 likewise to \(\mathrm{C_2H_5}\), Br, H and the C3 fragment. Both carry four different groups, so there are 2 chiral carbons.

93.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Acidity
93.solution: 2-Methylhexan-3-ol is \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}CH(OH){-}CH_2CH_2CH_3}\). Acid dehydration removes \(-\mathrm{OH}\) from C3 to give a secondary carbocation at C3, which rearranges by a 1,2-hydride shift to the more stable tertiary carbocation at C2. Loss of a proton (Saytzeff) gives the more substituted alkene 2-methylhex-2-ene, \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}CH{-}CH_2CH_2CH_3}\). Option A shows this trisubstituted alkene (terminal \(\mathrm{gem}\)-dimethyl carbon at the double bond).
93.note: Options are structure figures (option text blank). Read all four: A = 2-methylhex-2-ene (gem-dimethyl on the doubly-bonded carbon, the Saytzeff product after hydride shift to the tertiary cation); B/C/D are other hexene-skeleton isomers. Attaching the option figures.

94.subtopic: Reaction Mechanism, Intermediates and Rate-Determining Step
94.solution: An intermediate is produced in one step and consumed in a later step. \(\mathrm{ClO_2^{-}}\) is formed in step (i) and used up in step (ii), so it is the reaction intermediate. (\(\mathrm{ClO^{-}}\) is a reactant; \(\mathrm{ClO_3^{-}}\) and \(\mathrm{Cl^{-}}\) are products.)

95.subtopic: Group 2 Alkaline Earth Metals, Properties and Reactivity
95.solution: Magnesium burning in air reacts with both oxygen and nitrogen: \(\mathrm{2Mg + O_2 \to 2MgO}\) and \(\mathrm{3Mg + N_2 \to Mg_3N_2}\). So the products are MgO and \(\mathrm{Mg_3N_2}\).

96.solution: Number of atoms in \(0.4\) mol \(= 0.4 \times 6.022\times 10^{23} = 2.4088\times 10^{23}\). Octahedral voids \(=\) number of atoms \(= 2.4088\times 10^{23}\); tetrahedral voids \(= 2\times\) atoms \(= 4.8176\times 10^{23}\). Total \(= 2.4088\times 10^{23} + 4.8176\times 10^{23} = 7.2264\times 10^{23}\).

97.solution: On cyclisation of glucose, C1 (the former aldehyde carbon) becomes the new stereocentre bearing the hemiacetal \(-\mathrm{OH}\); this is the anomeric carbon. So C-1 is anomeric.

99.solution: A ketone gives a semicarbazone on reaction with semicarbazide, \(\mathrm{H_2N{-}NH{-}CONH_2}\). So reagent R is \(\mathrm{NH_2{-}NH{-}CONH_2}\). \(\mathrm{NH_2OH}\) gives an oxime, phenylhydrazine gives a phenylhydrazone, and hydrazine gives a hydrazone.

100.solution: Kolbe's reaction: sodium phenoxide is heated with \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) under pressure to give sodium salicylate, which on acidification gives salicylic acid. Hence substrate A is sodium phenoxide.

101.solution: For \(B(10,p)\), \(5P(X=0)=P(X=1)\) gives \(5q^{10}=10pq^{9}\Rightarrow q=2p\). With \(p+q=1\): \(3p=1\Rightarrow p=\dfrac13,\ q=\dfrac23\). Then \(\dfrac{P(X=5)}{P(X=6)}=\dfrac{^{10}C_5 p^5q^5}{^{10}C_6 p^6q^4}=\dfrac{^{10}C_5}{^{10}C_6}\cdot\dfrac{q}{p}=\dfrac{6}{5}\cdot2=\dfrac{12}{5}\).

102.solution: Put \(u=x+9y\Rightarrow \dfrac{du}{dx}=1+9u^2\), so \(\dfrac{du}{1+9u^2}=dx\). Integrating: \(\dfrac13\tan^{-1}(3u)=x+c\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}(3x+27y)=3x+3c\). At \(x=0,\ y=\dfrac1{27}\): \(\tan^{-1}(1)=3c\Rightarrow 3c=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\). Hence \(3x+27y=\tan\!\left(3x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\tan\!\left[3\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)\right]\).

103.solution: As \(x\to\infty\), \(e^{x^4}\to\infty\). Divide numerator and denominator by \(e^{x^4}\): \(\dfrac{1-e^{-x^4}}{1+e^{-x^4}}\to\dfrac{1-0}{1+0}=1\).

104.solution: \(\bar b_1\times\bar b_2=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\1&2&-3\\2&4&-5\end{vmatrix}=(2,-1,0)\), magnitude \(\sqrt5\). \(\bar a_2-\bar a_1=(\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k)-(4\hat i-\hat j)=(-3,0,2)\). Shortest distance \(=\left|\dfrac{(-3,0,2)\cdot(2,-1,0)}{\sqrt5}\right|=\left|\dfrac{-6}{\sqrt5}\right|=\dfrac{6}{\sqrt5}\) units.

105.solution: With \(f(x)=\cos(\log x)\), let \(A=\log x^2,\ B=\log y^2\). Then \(f(x^2)f(y^2)=\cos A\cos B\). Also \(f\!\left(\dfrac{x^2}{y^2}\right)=\cos(A-B)\) and \(f(x^2y^2)=\cos(A+B)\). The expression is \(\cos A\cos B-\dfrac12[\cos(A-B)+\cos(A+B)]=\cos A\cos B-\dfrac12(2\cos A\cos B)=0\).

106.solution: Separate: \(\dfrac{dy}{y}=2x e^{x^2}dx\). Put \(u=x^2\): \(\log y=\int e^u\,du=e^{x^2}+\log c\Rightarrow \log\dfrac{y}{c}=e^{x^2}\Rightarrow y=c\,e^{e^{x^2}}\).

107.solution: A function \(f(x,y)\) is homogeneous of degree \(n\) if \(f(\lambda x,\lambda y)=\lambda^n f(x,y)\). \(y^2+2xy\) (degree 2), \(2x-3y\) (degree 1), and \(\sin(y/x)\) (degree 0) all satisfy this. But \(\cos x+\sin y\) does not, so it is not homogeneous.

108.solution: Volume \(=\begin{vmatrix}1&x&1\\0&1&x\\x&0&1\end{vmatrix}=1(1)-x(0-x^2)+1(0-x)=1+x^3-x\). Let \(f(x)=1+x^3-x\); \(f'(x)=3x^2-1=0\Rightarrow x=\pm\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\). \(f''(x)=6x\): max at \(x=-\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\), min at \(x=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\). Max \(=1+\dfrac{2}{3\sqrt3}\), min \(=1-\dfrac{2}{3\sqrt3}\).

109.subtopic: Probability Distribution — Constants, Expectation, and Variance
109.solution: Non-negativity of all probabilities gives \(0\le p\le1\), so minimum \(p=0\). \(E(X)=0\cdot\dfrac{1+p}5+1\cdot\dfrac{2-2p}5+2\cdot\dfrac{2-p}5+3\cdot\dfrac{2p}5=\dfrac{6+2p}5\). Hence \(5E(X)=6+2p\); at \(p=0\), \(5E(X)=6\).

110.subtopic: Scalar Triple Product, Coplanarity, and Volume
110.solution: Expand \(\bar a\times(\bar b\times\bar c)=(\bar a\cdot\bar c)\bar b-(\bar a\cdot\bar b)\bar c\). Dotting with \(\bar a\times\bar c\): the \(\bar c\) term vanishes (\(\bar c\cdot(\bar a\times\bar c)=0\)), giving \((\bar a\cdot\bar c)\,[\bar b\;\bar a\;\bar c]=5\). Since \(\bar a\cdot\bar c=\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac12\), \([\bar b\;\bar a\;\bar c]=10\). Thus \([\bar a\;\bar b\;\bar c]=-[\bar b\;\bar a\;\bar c]=-10\).

111.subtopic: Probability Distribution — Constants, Expectation, and Variance

112.subtopic: Area Bounded by Curves, Axes, and Lines
112.solution: Area \(=2\int_a^{4a}\sqrt{4ax}\,dx=4\sqrt a\cdot\dfrac23\left[x^{3/2}\right]_a^{4a}=\dfrac8{3}\sqrt a\left[(4a)^{3/2}-a^{3/2}\right]=\dfrac8{3}\sqrt a\,(8a\sqrt a-a\sqrt a)=\dfrac8{3}\sqrt a\cdot7a\sqrt a=\dfrac{56}{3}a^2\) sq. units.

113.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value
113.solution: Let \(I=\int_2^4\dfrac{\log x^2}{\log x^2+\log(6-x)^2}\,dx\) (since \(36-12x+x^2=(6-x)^2\)). By King's property \(x\to6-x\): \(I=\int_2^4\dfrac{\log(6-x)^2}{\log(6-x)^2+\log x^2}\,dx\). Adding, \(2I=\int_2^4 1\,dx=2\Rightarrow I=1\).

114.solution: Since \(\bar a\cdot\bar b=\bar a\cdot\bar c=0\), \(\bar a\) is perpendicular to both \(\bar b\) and \(\bar c\), so \(\bar a=\pm\dfrac{\bar b\times\bar c}{|\bar b\times\bar c|}\). Here \(|\bar b\times\bar c|=\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac12\), giving \(\bar a=\pm2(\bar b\times\bar c)\).

115.solution: \(|\bar a+\bar b|^2=1+1+2\bar a\cdot\bar b=3\Rightarrow \bar a\cdot\bar b=\dfrac12\). Since \(\bar a\cdot\bar b=\cos\theta=\dfrac12\), \(\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\).

116.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value

117.subtopic: Trigonometric Integrals - Rational and Substitution Forms
117.solution: Put \(u=4\sin x+7\Rightarrow \sin x=\dfrac{u-7}4,\ \cos x\,dx=\dfrac{du}4\). Then \(I=\dfrac3{16}\int\dfrac{u-7}{u}\,du=\dfrac3{16}(u-7\log u)=\dfrac3{16}(4\sin x+7)-\dfrac{21}{16}\log(4\sin x+7)=\dfrac34\sin x-\dfrac{21}{16}\log(4\sin x+7)+c\). So \(A=\dfrac34,\ B=\dfrac{21}{16}\), and \(A+B=\dfrac{33}{16}\).

118.subtopic: Scalar Triple Product, Coplanarity, and Volume
118.solution: Volume \(=\begin{vmatrix}1&0&-1\\\lambda&1&1-\lambda\\\mu&\lambda&1+\lambda-\mu\end{vmatrix}\). Applying \(C_3\to C_3+C_1\): \(\begin{vmatrix}1&0&0\\\lambda&1&1\\\mu&\lambda&1+\lambda\end{vmatrix}=1\cdot(1+\lambda-\lambda)=1\), which is independent of both \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\).

120.subtopic: Combined Equation and Condition for Pair of Lines
120.solution: The lines \(x=5\) (vertical) and \(y=3\) (horizontal) meet at \((5,3)\); their angle bisectors pass through \((5,3)\) with slopes \(\pm1\): \(y-3=\pm(x-5)\), i.e. \(x-y-2=0\) and \(x+y-8=0\). Joint equation: \((x-y-2)(x+y-8)=x^2-y^2-10x+6y+16=0\).

121.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Identities, Equations, Principal Values, and Sums

122.solution: Complete the square: \(x^2-6x-16=(x-3)^2-25\). Using \(\int\sqrt{t^2-a^2}\,dt=\dfrac t2\sqrt{t^2-a^2}-\dfrac{a^2}2\log\left|t+\sqrt{t^2-a^2}\right|\) with \(t=x-3,\ a^2=25\): \(I=\dfrac{x-3}2\sqrt{x^2-6x-16}-\dfrac{25}2\log\left(x-3+\sqrt{x^2-6x-16}\right)+c\).

123.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Identities, Equations, Principal Values, and Sums

124.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection

125.solution: Line–line intersections: \(^8C_2=28\). Circle–circle: each pair meets in at most 2 points, \(2\cdot{}^4C_2=12\). Line–circle: each of \(8\times4=32\) pairs meets in at most 2 points, \(64\). Total \(=28+12+64=104\).

126.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection
126.solution: \(a\cos B=b\cos A\) with the cosine rule gives \(a^2+c^2-b^2=b^2+c^2-a^2\Rightarrow a=b\). Area \(=\dfrac12 a^2\sin C\). From \(c^2=2a^2(1-\cos C)\), \(\cos C=\dfrac{2a^2-c^2}{2a^2}\), so \(\sin C=\dfrac{c\sqrt{4a^2-c^2}}{2a^2}\). Hence Area \(=\dfrac12 a^2\cdot\dfrac{c\sqrt{4a^2-c^2}}{2a^2}=\dfrac c4\sqrt{4a^2-c^2}\).

127.subtopic: Rate of Change and Related Rates
127.solution: Lateral surface area \(A=\pi r\sqrt{r^2+h^2}\). \(\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\pi\left[\dfrac{r(r\,r'+h\,h')}{\sqrt{r^2+h^2}}+\sqrt{r^2+h^2}\,r'\right]\). With \(r=7,h=24,\ \sqrt{r^2+h^2}=25,\ r'=3,h'=-4\): \(\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\pi\left[\dfrac{7(21-96)}{25}+25\cdot3\right]=\pi[-21+75]=54\pi\) cm\(^2\)/min.

128.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection
128.solution: \(c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C=16+64-64\cdot\dfrac12=48\Rightarrow c=4\sqrt3\). \(\cos B=\dfrac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2ac}=\dfrac{16+48-64}{32\sqrt3}=0\Rightarrow B=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\). \(\cos A=\dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc}=\dfrac{96}{64\sqrt3}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\), \(\cos C=\dfrac12\), so \(\cos A:\cos C=\sqrt3:1\).

129.solution: With \(a_{ij}=2i+j\): \(A=\begin{bmatrix}3&4&5\\5&6&7\\7&8&9\end{bmatrix}\). The third element in the second row of \(\operatorname{adj}A\) is \((\operatorname{adj}A)_{23}=C_{32}=(-1)^{3+2}\begin{vmatrix}3&5\\5&7\end{vmatrix}=-(21-25)=4\).

132.subtopic: Rolle's Theorem and Mean Value Theorem

138.solution: \([\sim(\sim p\vee q)\vee(p\wedge r)]\wedge(\sim q\wedge r)\). By De Morgan, \(\sim(\sim p\vee q)=p\wedge\sim q\), so the bracket is \((p\wedge\sim q)\vee(p\wedge r)=p\wedge(\sim q\vee r)\). Then \(p\wedge(\sim q\vee r)\wedge(\sim q\wedge r)\); since \(\sim q\wedge r\) implies \(\sim q\vee r\), this reduces to \(p\wedge\sim q\wedge r=(p\wedge r)\wedge\sim q\).
